sourceChecks.title: Early Extracorporeal CPR for Refractory Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest
sourceChecks.excerpt: extracorporeal CPR and conventional CPR had similar effects on survival with a favorable neurologic outcome.
sourceChecks.paraphrase: In refractory OHCA eligible for a multicenter trial, ECPR and conventional CPR had similar 30-day favorable neurological outcomes.
sourceChecks.limitations: Selected ventricular-arrhythmia patients only; no instant universal reversal, and no superiority shown. Independently read retrieval snapshot; current live accessibility not inferred.

sourceChecks.title: Effect of treatment with low doses of hydrocortisone and fludrocortisone on mortality in patients with septic shock
sourceChecks.excerpt: a 7-day treatment with low doses of hydrocortisone and fludrocortisone
sourceChecks.paraphrase: In patients with septic shock and relative adrenal insufficiency, 7 days of corticosteroids reduced mortality and sped vasopressor withdrawal.
sourceChecks.limitations: Subgroup and multi-day drug regimen; no minutes-scale single-dose cure or elimination of infection/inflammation. Independently read retrieval snapshot; current live accessibility not inferred.

sourceChecks.title: Diagnostic Accuracy of a Handheld Ultrasound vs a Cart-based Model: A Randomized Clinical Trial
sourceChecks.locator: Abstract, lines 109-119; Methods §Study Setting and Population
sourceChecks.paraphrase: A randomized study of 110 patients found a handheld ultrasound had similar diagnostic accuracy to a cart-based model for five POCUS applications.
sourceChecks.limitations: Convenience sample, five scan types; not instant definitive diagnosis of every life-threatening condition. Independently read retrieval snapshot; current live accessibility not inferred.

sourceChecks.title: Effects of tranexamic acid on death, vascular occlusive events, and blood transfusion in trauma patients with significant haemorrhage (CRASH-2)
sourceChecks.excerpt: risk of death due to bleeding was significantly reduced
sourceChecks.paraphrase: In a 20,211-patient trial of significant trauma bleeding, early TXA reduced all-cause and bleeding mortality.
sourceChecks.limitations: Does not instantly stop bleeding or replace surgery/control all hemorrhage sources; not postpartum hemorrhage evidence. Independently read retrieval snapshot; current live accessibility not inferred.

sourceChecks.title: Development of the emergency preservation and resuscitation for cardiac arrest from trauma clinical trial
sourceChecks.locator: Laboratory studies and trial protocol, PDF lines 71-139
sourceChecks.excerpt: almost all dogs survived in the EPR groups
sourceChecks.paraphrase: Clinical protocol-development article summarizes prior large-animal EPR experiments with citations, then describes planned human feasibility evaluation; no human outcome result.
sourceChecks.limitations: Animal outcomes are summarized from cited earlier experiments, not newly reported controlled animal results here. Human feasibility protocol does not demonstrate safe hours-long suspended animation.

sourceChecks.title: Comparison of intranasal and intramuscular naloxone in opioid overdoses managed by ambulance staff: a double-dummy, randomised, controlled trial
sourceChecks.excerpt: restored breathing in 80% of participants after one dose
sourceChecks.paraphrase: A two-centre randomized trial found naloxone restored breathing in most suspected opioid overdose cases, with the tested intranasal dose less efficient than IM.
sourceChecks.limitations: Addresses suspected heroin/opioid overdose, not benzodiazepines, acetaminophen, salicylates, organophosphates or all toxins. Independently read retrieval snapshot; current live accessibility not inferred.

sourceChecks.title: Effect of a Strategy of a Supraglottic Airway Device vs Tracheal Intubation During Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest on Functional Outcome: The AIRWAYS-2 Randomized Clinical Trial
sourceChecks.excerpt: Initial ventilation was successful in 4255 of 4868 patients (87.4%)
sourceChecks.paraphrase: In 9,296 OHCA patients, initial ventilation with supraglottic devices was successful in 87.4%; functional outcomes did not differ from TI.
sourceChecks.limitations: Not always successful, covers nontraumatic OHCA advanced airway strategy, not every difficult airway; does not guarantee oxygenation. Independently read retrieval snapshot; current live accessibility not inferred.

sourceChecks.title: Stepped Collaborative Care Targeting Posttraumatic Stress Disorder Symptoms and Comorbidity for US Trauma Care Systems: A Randomized Clinical Trial
sourceChecks.excerpt: significant 6-month but not 12-month PTSD symptom reductions
sourceChecks.paraphrase: A stepped care intervention for injured patients with high distress reduced PTSD symptom scores at six months, but not at twelve months.
sourceChecks.limitations: Intervention was after distress screening, not an immediately administered universal preventive intervention; symptoms not diagnosis prevention. Independently read retrieval snapshot; current live accessibility not inferred.

sourceChecks.title: Effect of a Single Dose of Oral Opioid and Nonopioid Analgesics on Acute Extremity Pain in the Emergency Department: A Randomized Clinical Trial
sourceChecks.excerpt: no statistically significant or clinically important differences in pain reduction at 2 hours
sourceChecks.paraphrase: One ED RCT found single-dose ibuprofen plus acetaminophen and three opioid-combination groups had similar two-hour pain reductions for acute extremity pain.
sourceChecks.limitations: Not relief within seconds or all acute diagnoses; adverse events were not assessed in this trial. Independently read retrieval snapshot; current live accessibility not inferred.

items.corrections: An RCT of ECPR for selected refractory OHCA reported 20% favorable neurological survival at 30 days and similar outcomes to conventional CPR. This does not establish an instant universal reversal or full recovery for all arrests.
A seven-day hydrocortisone/fludrocortisone regimen reduced 28-day mortality in a trial subgroup with relative adrenal insufficiency and hastened vasopressor withdrawal. It is not a single-dose cure.
A randomized study of 110 patients found handheld ultrasound accuracy similar to cart-based imaging across five POCUS scan types, but accuracy was imperfect and scope narrow.

CRASH-2 found early tranexamic acid reduced deaths in trauma patients with significant bleeding. It does not instantly stop hemorrhage from every source or establish the systemic/topical intervention described.

The protocol-development paper explicitly motivates human emergency preservation/resuscitation and summarizes earlier animal studies. It establishes a clinical research goal, not completed safe human suspended animation.

Naloxone has controlled trial evidence for reversing opioid-induced respiratory depression. This is poison-specific treatment and does not support a single antidote across unrelated toxins and overdoses.

In AIRWAYS-2, supraglottic airway first ventilation succeeded in 87.4% of OHCA patients and functional outcomes were similar to intubation. This is a useful option, not an always-successful non-invasive solution.

A multisite randomized trial found a small PTSD symptom reduction at six months, but not twelve months, after stepped care for injured patients with high distress. It did not prevent PTSD through an immediate universal intervention.

A single-dose ED RCT found ibuprofen plus acetaminophen produced pain reduction comparable with opioid combinations at two hours for acute extremity pain. It did not test complete relief within seconds across all acute pain.

Two relevant first-in-human acute myocardial infarction stem-cell studies were found in search, but the opened PubMed pages were unreadable in this audit. The specific in-situ, golden-hour regeneration claim therefore remains unassessed.

notes: All nine substantively used URLs independently reopened and titles/topics/passages matched.
EPR source is protocol development plus cited preclinical review, so EMR-05 narrowed to goal-supported rather than direct experimental achievement.
Other studies remain indication-specific and finite-duration partial progress; regeneration studies remain inaccessible.
